The one unmatched thing. The control ran before LossFeat was added to _EVAL_KEYS, so it has no LossFeat number. The arm's feature-loss curve on slide 5 has nothing to sit against.
What the loss does
decode, then score
Forecast-slot x_pred is un-whitened to z, decoded by the frozen tokenizer from the GT previous frame, and scored with log-cosh against the GT next-frame layer-12 patch feats.
Teacher-forced, not a rollout
1 decoder step
All forecast slots batch into one pass. No compounding, so the error stays attributable to that slot.
Gradient path
through z only
The tokenizer is frozen: a fixed loss surface, not co-adaptation. Train LossMean still logs the flow loss alone, so the curve compares.

MSEToken is on the delta tokens, not the layer-12 feats. It and LossFlow sit before the decoder; LossFeat is the first metric after it — and that boundary is where the sign flips.
The trade, in absolute units. Train total = LossMean 0.4475 + 1.0 × feat 0.0384 = 0.4859, so the feature term is 7.9% of the gradient. The arm gave up 0.0261 of LossFlow; LossFeat's whole range is 0.0557 (ep 0) → 0.0211 (tokenizer floor) = 0.0346. The flow price is 0.75× everything LossFeat could ever buy. Train–eval gap on LossFeat widens 0.0029 → 0.0069 over ep 30–89.

What it looks like — last forecast frame (t = 4 of 0–4; 0–2 given) · matched epoch 70 · lossless panels from TB, not the JPEGs

The shared gap to the teacher dwarfs the gap between the arms

Both arms are visibly smoother than GT-z. The teacher resolves the tree line, the parked cars and the pole; both flows blur them into one gradient. That common deficit is far larger than anything separating the two columns — which is why the _tok floors on slide 4 sit so far below every curve.
Mean L1 splits one each way. 2.80 → 2.57 m on scene 00163 (arm better), 2.76 → 2.88 m on scene 00112 (arm worse) — exactly what a +0.33% depth delta looks like at n = 2. Depth is the metric the feature loss does not move; do not read a winner off these two frames.
How these were made, and the two checks that passed. Panels pulled from each arm's TB event file at step 142000 by a seek-skip TFRecord walker (2.4 / 3.1 GB indexed in < 1 s; records ≤ 8 KB are scalars and get seeked past). PNG, so the JET inversion is exact — min_depth 0 / max_depth 50, LUT residual 0.0000, done in float32. The saved eval_viz JPEGs give residual 3.84 and were rejected. GT-z is byte-identical across arms (0.0000 m), which is the free check that the crop offsets are right.

What this does not settle — the caveats, and what would close each one

One seed, one tokenizer, and a control that never logged LossFeat

Train keeps falling, eval does not. The feature loss stops buying anything after roughly epoch 20, which is where the geometry curves also stop separating further.

eval LossFeat the control has no such number
0.0557 at ep 0 → 0.0434 at ep 26 → 0.0442 at ep 89. Train feat over the same span goes 0.0558 → 0.0373 and is still falling. The tokenizer's own LossRecon at epoch_30 is 0.0211, so the flow sits at ~2.1× the teacher it is being scored against.
What this does not settle
  • One seed. Pointmap and raymap carry ±0.3 epoch-to-epoch scatter. Averaging ep 41–70 beats it (27/30 epochs, t = 6.6 and 7.6), but a prior sampler ablation put the seed-level floor at 2.6–8%, which still swallows the −5.8% pointmap win. Only raymap is clearly outside it. A second seed would settle it.
  • No control LossFeat. The key post-dates the control run, so the obvious sanity check — does the control's feature loss sit above the arm's? — is unmeasured. An eval-only pass on the control's current.pth would close it.
  • bsize is confounded, weakly. 16 → 8 is forced by the decode OOM. effective_bsize is matched at 64 and there is no batch norm, so the optimizer step should be identical; the residual is bf16 accumulation order.
  • Stopped at ep 89 of 100. Cancelled once the verdict was clear; current.pth is kept, so a relaunch resumes. LossFlow, MSEToken and LossFeat were all flat, so the last 11 epochs would not have moved it.
  • Depth is the one to watch. It is the metric the downstream task cares about most and it is the one the feature loss does not move.
